The case claims that the law’s voting restrictions — including new identification requirements for absentee voting, limits on the use of absentee drop boxes, invalidating ballots cast before 5:00 p.m. in the wrong precinct, banning any non-poll worker from giving food or drink, including water, to voters waiting in line and more — violate the First, 14th and 15th Amendments and Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. The Republican National Committee (RNC), National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC), National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC) and Georgia Republican Party intervened in the case to protect S.B. 202.

STATUS: The case was administratively closed after being consolidated with five others bringing similar claims against S.B. 202. All future filings and updates can be found in In re: Georgia Senate Bill 202.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging Georgia voter suppression law S.B. 202.
title: Georgia Voter Suppression Law (New Georgia Project)
body:
Lawsuit brought by the New Georgia Project, Black Voters Matter Fund and Rise challenging several provisions of Georgia voter suppression law Senate Bill 202. The case claims that the law’s voting restrictions — including new identification requirements for absentee voting, limits on the use of absentee drop boxes, banning mobile polling places, invalidating ballots cast before 5:00 p.m. in the wrong precinct, banning any non-poll worker from giving food or drink, including water, to voters waiting in line and more — violate the 14th Amendment and Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. The Republican National Committee (RNC), National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) and Georgia Republican Party intervened in the case to protect S.B. 202.

STATUS: The case was administratively closed after being consolidated with five others bringing similar claims against S.B. 202. All future filings and updates can be found in In re: Georgia Senate Bill 202.

parties: Texas Alliance for Retired Americans v. Abbott
excerpt: Lawsuit challenging the limit on locations to return mail-in and absentee ballots during the 2020 election cycle in Texas.
title: Texas Ballot Return Restriction
body: Consolidated lawsuit filed by various voting rights groups challenging Texas Governor Greg Abbott’s (R) October announcement that, despite an expansion of early voting earlier during the COVID-19 pandemic, Texas counties could only provide one location per county to deliver mail-in and absentee ballots. The complaint challenges the constitutionality of this order, which would effectively close additional drop box locations throughout the state. The district court agreed with the plaintiffs and blocked the Governor from enforcing his order. On appeal to the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, the district court’s preliminary injunction was stayed pending appeal — effectively allowing Abbott’s ban on additional drop boxes to remain in place for the November 2020 election. Months after the election the district court dismissed the case as moot, per the order of the 5th Circuit.

excerpt: Lawsuit brought by the state of Ohio against the U.S. Census Bureau challenging the delayed release of census data to the states.
title: Ohio Census Delay Challenge
body: Lawsuit brought by the state of Ohio against the U.S. Census Bureau challenging the delayed release of census data to the states. The lawsuit asked the court to declare that the Bureau violated the Census Act. The court denied the state’s motion for a preliminary injunction and dismissed the case for lack of jurisdiction.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging multiple aspects of Georgia’s voting procedures ahead of the 2020 general election.
title: Georgia COVID-19 Election Relief
body: Lawsuit filed on behalf of the New Georgia Project and individual voters challenging multiple aspect of Georgia’s voting procedures — including its failure to provide prepaid postage for mail-in ballots, Election Day receipt deadline, voter assistance ban and lack of standards for notifying voters about incomplete absentee ballot applications — for posing an undue burden on the right to vote generally and particularly during the 2020 general election due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The district court extended the ballot receipt deadline, but denied the plaintiffs’ motion for a preliminary injunction as to their other requests. The state defendants appealed this order to the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, which stayed (paused) the district court’s injunction extending the ballot receipt deadline. The parties dismissed the case.

excerpt: Trump lawsuit challenging the 2020 presidential election results in Wisconsin.
title: Wisconsin Federal Election Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Trump campaign challenging the results of the 2020 election in Wisconsin. Specifically, Trump asked the district court to “declare the election a failure, with the results discarded, and the door thus opened for the Wisconsin Legislature to appoint Presidential Electors in some fashion other than by following the certified voting results.” The Democratic National Committee (DNC) and NAACP intervened in the case to protect the election results. The district court dismissed the case with prejudice, writing that a “sitting president who did not prevail in his bid for reelection has asked for federal court help in setting aside the popular vote based on disputed issues of election administration.” After Trump appealed, the 7th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court’s decision and the U.S. Supreme Court declined to grant Trump’s petition.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Democratic lawsuit challenging two Montana voting restrictions.
title: Montana Absentee Ballot Collection
body: Lawsuit brought by the Montana Democratic Party and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee challenging two voting restrictions: a law that restricts ballot collection and a requirement that absentee ballots must be received by the county elections office by 8 p.m. on Election Day. The trial court granted a preliminary injunction blocking state officials from implementing the challenged laws. The Montana Supreme Court affirmed the preliminary injunction against the ballot collection restriction, but vacated the district court’s order and set the absentee ballot deadline to 8 p.m. on Election Day.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to decertify the 2020 presidential election results in Wisconsin.
title: Wisconsin Decertification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by a Trump elector for Wisconsin and a Republican congressional candidate seeking to decertify the 2020 general election results in Wisconsin, or have the court order the governor to transmit only stating Trump is the winner, based on allegations of illegal misconduct by the Wisconsin Elections Commission and fraud due to Dominion voting machines. The district court dismissed the case, pointing out that “Federal judges do not appoint the president of the country” and therefore the court has no jurisdiction or authority to grant the requested relief. The U.S. Supreme Court denied the petitions for writs of mandamus.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to vacate the certification of 2020 presidential election results in Arizona.
title: Arizona Decertification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit brought by Republican electors in Arizona against the Arizona governor and secretary of state seeking to decertify the 2020 presidential election results. The U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona dismissed the case and the U.S. Supreme Court denied a subsequent writ of mandamus.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit challenging the 2020 presidential election results in Georgia.
title: Georgia Presidential Electors Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by pro-Trump lawyer and conspiracy theorist L. Lin Wood challenging the inclusion of absentee ballots in the general election results of Georgia. The Democratic Party of Georgia, Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) successfully intervened in the case. The district court denied Wood’s motion for injunctive relief due to lack of standing, which Wood immediately appealed to the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. The 11th Circuit affirmed the district court’s denial of injunctive relief and the U.S. Supreme Court denied Wood’s petition for a writ of certiorari. The case was dismissed with prejudice.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit filed by the Pennsylvania Democratic Party and voters seeking to protect and expand mail-in voting for the 2020 general election.
title: Pennsylvania COVID-19 Vote By Mail Expansion
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Pennsylvania Democratic Party and voters against the Pennsylvania secretary of state and all 67 county board of elections seeking to protect and expand mail-in voting for the 2020 general election. Specifically, the plaintiffs asked the state court for a ruling that drop boxes are permitted; ballots mailed by Election Day but received up to one week after must be counted; election officials must provide meaningful notice and opportunity for voters to cure deficient mail-in ballots; “naked” ballots (mail-in ballots returned without an outer secrecy envelope) must be counted; and that Pennsylvania’s poll watcher residency requirement doesn’t violate federal law. The Pennsylvania Supreme Court took over the case, agreeing with the plaintiffs that drop boxes are permitted under Pennsylvania law and the poll watcher residency requirement is constitutional. The court also extended the ballot receipt deadline by three days so that ballots cast by 8 p.m. on Election Day, (Nov. 3, 2020) and received by 5 p.m. on Nov. 6, 2020 would be counted. The court rejected the plaintiffs’ two remaining requests.

Republican legislative leaders immediately went to the U.S. Supreme Court asking it to pause the Pennsylvania Supreme Court’s three-day extension of the ballot receipt deadline. The U.S. Supreme Court denied this request. Soon after, the Republican Party of Pennsylvania similarly went to the Court to ask it to segregate mail-in ballots received after 8 p.m. on Election Day through Nov. 6, 2020 so that these ballots were not included in final vote counts pending the resolution of litigation. Justice Samuel Alito granted this request, ordering the segregation and separate vote tally of these ballots.

excerpt: Trump lawsuit alleging fraud in the 2020 presidential election in Wisconsin and requesting a recount.
title: Wisconsin 2020 Election Recount (Milwaukee & Dane County)
body:
Petition filed by President Donald Trump, Vice President Mike Pence and the Trump campaign against Joe Biden and Kamala Harris claiming fraud in the Wisconsin 2020 presidential election and requesting a recount in Milwaukee and Dane counties. The trial court affirmed the counties’ certification of presidential results, as did the Wisconsin Supreme Court. The U.S. Supreme Court declined to grant Trump’s petition.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit brought by the Trump campaign against the Philadelphia Board of Elections arguing that the election commissioners did not provide Republican poll observers “meaningful access” to observe the canvassing process of absentee and mail-in ballots at the Philadelphia Convention Center in accordance with Pennsylvania law.
title: Pennsylvania Philadelphia Canvassing Observation Challenge
body:
Lawsuit brought by the Trump campaign against the Philadelphia Board of Elections arguing that the election commissioners did not provide Republican poll observers “meaningful access” to observe the canvassing process of absentee and mail-in ballots at the Philadelphia Convention Center in accordance with Pennsylvania law. After hearing testimony from a witness, the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas found that the observation allowed for the Trump campaign “complied with the relevant provisions of the Election Code” and denied the petition. The Trump campaign appealed this decision to the Commonwealth Court, which reversed the Court of Common Pleas’ opinion and remanded the case back to it. Then, the Philadelphia Board of Elections filed an emergency petition with the Pennsylvania Supreme Court asking “to accept emergency review to consider the Commonwealth Court’s decision of first-impression.” On Nov. 17, 2020, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court vacated (meaning voided) the Commonwealth Court’s decision and reinstated the Court of Common Pleas’ order denying the Trump campaign’s request for expanded observation access. The Trump campaign filed a petition for writ of certiorari — which invoked the radical independent state legislature theory — in the U.S. Supreme Court, but the petition was denied on Feb. 22, 2021.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to block the certification of 2020 presidential election results in Arizona.
title: Arizona Election Contest
body:
Lawsuit brought by Republican politician Kelli Ward against the Biden electors of Arizona seeking to block certification of the 2020 presidential election. The Superior Court rejected the requested relief; Ward appealed to the Supreme Court of Arizona, which affirmed the lower court’s ruling, and then to the U.S. Supreme Court, which denied her petition for writ of certiorari.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. v. Boockvar
excerpt: Trump lawsuit challenging the 2020 presidential election results in various Democratic counties in Pennsylvania.
title: Pennsylvania Democratic Counties Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Trump campaign against the Pennsylvania secretary of the commonwealth and county boards of elections challenging the election results in various Democratic counties based on allegations that the elections officials violated the state election code by not enacting enough “procedural safeguards to deter fraud and ensure transparency” regarding the processing of mail-in ballots and not allowing poll watchers observe the process. The district court denied the plaintiffs’ request for injunctive relief and dismissed the case, writing that the Trump campaign presented “strained legal arguments without merit and speculative accusations.” Upon appeal, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied the Trump campaign’s motion for injunctive relief and affirmed the district court’s decision barring the Trump campaign from filing another amended complaint. The Trump campaign petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court, which declined to review the petition on an expedited basis, meaning that the 3rd Circuit’s ruling remained in place and the Pennsylvania election results were certified. The Supreme Court later denied the petition.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to block the certification of the 2020 presidential election results in Pennsylvania.
title: Pennsylvania Vote By Mail Certification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by several Republican candidates and individual voters against Pennsylvania, the General Assembly, Gov. Tim Wolf (D) and Pennsylvania Secretary of State Kathy Boockvar (D) seeking to block Pennsylvania’s certification of presidential election results. Specifically, the suit asked the court to exclude mail-in ballots from the certified results or alternatively direct the General Assembly to choose its own electors. The appellate court enjoined the state from certifying remaining results pending an evidentiary hearing, which the state supreme court promptly vacated and dismissed the case. The Republican candidates and voters appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court, which denied their petition.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to block the counting of absentee ballots in Detroit, Michigan.
title: Michigan Election Integrity Oversight Process
body:
Lawsuit filed by an individual voter and the conservative group Election Integrity Fund seeking to block the counting of absentee ballots in Detroit. The Democratic National Committee (DNC) intervened in the case. The court denied the plaintiffs’ request for a preliminary injunction and later granted a motion to dismiss the case.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: On Feb. 22, 2021, the case was dismissed. Detroit’s absentee ballots were counted.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to decertify Michigan’s 2020 presidential election results.
title: Michigan Decertification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by individual Republican voters seeking to decertify Michigan’s 2020 presidential election results based on allegations that there were “hundreds of thousands of illegal, ineligible, duplicate or purely fictitious ballots” cast. The district court denied the plaintiffs’ request for injunctive relief, writing that the lawsuit was “less about achieving the relief Plaintiffs seek — as much of that relief is beyond the power of this Court — and more about the impact of their allegations on People’s faith in the democratic process and their trust in our government,” and dismissed the case. The voters appealed the decision to the 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, but due to “exigencies of time” they then petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court before the 6th Circuit heard the case. The Supreme Court denied the petition. Various parties moved for sanctions of the plaintiffs’ lawyers, which were granted by the district court.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: On Feb. 22, 2021, the U.S. Supreme Court denied the plaintiffs’ petition. Michigan’s 2020 presidential election results remain certified.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking a voter purge of Michigan’s voter rolls before the 2020 general election.
title: Michigan Voter Purge
body:
Lawsuit filed by an individual voter attempting to initiate a broad voter purge of Michigan’s voter rolls less than two months before the 2020 general election. A. Philip Randolph Institute and Rise Inc. intervened as defendants in the case.

RESULT: On Feb. 16, 2021, the parties agreed to dismiss the lawsuit after the Michigan secretary of state announced various “election security” initiatives.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to preserve election data and machines for an audit of the 2020 general election results in Michigan.
title: Michigan Election Materials Preservation
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Barry County sheriff and individual voters against Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer (D), Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson (D) and the state board of elections seeking to maintain and preserve election data and machines for a post-election audit. The district court denied the plaintiffs’ motion for a restraining order and the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: On Feb. 6, 2021, the case was dismissed.

parties: Tenney v. Oswego County Board of Elections
excerpt: Republican lawsuit challenging the outcome of New York’s 22nd Congressional District election.
title: New York 22nd Congressional District Challenge
body: Petition filed by Republican congressional candidate Claudia Tenney challenging the outcome of New York’s 22nd Congressional District election in which incumbent Democrat Anthony Brindisi was initially declared the winner. In her petition, Tenney challenged the validity of certain affidavit and absentee ballots. The state Supreme Court ordered the board of elections to recanvass all ballots in the district. Tenney was eventually declared the winner, winning 109 more votes than Brindisi.

parties: Majority Forward v. Ben Hill County
excerpt: Lawsuit filed against two Georgia counties for challenging voters’ eligibility ahead of the 2021 Senate runoff elections.
title: Georgia Muscogee County Voter Challenge
body: Lawsuit brought by Majority Forward and individual Georgia voters against Muscogee and Ben Hill County Boards for challenging the eligibility of over 4,000 voters ahead of the Georgia Senate runoff elections. The district court granted a preliminary injunction against Muscogee County blocking it from upholding any challenges based on certain criteria and requiring it to properly advise voters whose eligibility was challenged. The plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.

parties: North Carolina Alliance for Retired Americans v. North Carolina
excerpt: Lawsuit challenging North Carolina’s vote by mail and in-person voting options for the 2020 general election.
title: North Carolina November 2020 Election Challenge
body: Lawsuit filed on behalf of the North Carolina Alliance for Retired Americans and individual voters challenging the state’s vote by mail restrictions and in-person voting options for the 2020 general election. The parties entered a consent decree addressing issues raised in the complaints and the state agreed to extend ballot receipt deadlines, issue new cure guidance and expand absentee ballot drop off locations. State Republican legislative leaders along with the Republican National Committee, National Republican Senatorial Committee, National Republican Congressional Committee, North Carolina Republican Party and Trump campaign intervened in the case as defendants seeking to pause the enforcement of the consent decree pending appeal. Both the North Carolina Court of Appeals and Supreme Court denied their motions and their appeal was withdrawn. The case was dismissed.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to decertify the 2020 presidential election results in Georgia.
title: Georgia Decertification Challenge #1
body:
Lawsuit filed by individual voters seeking to decertify Georgia’s election results based on allegations that Dominion Voting equipment “rigged” the election in favor of President Joe Biden. The district court partially granted the plaintiffs’ request for a temporary restraining order asking the state to preserve election materials, but did not grant their request to block the transmission of certified election results, which the plaintiffs immediately appealed to the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. The 11th Circuit dismissed the appeal for lack of jurisdiction as the plaintiffs had appealed a non-final order, sending the case back down to the district court to continue. The district court then dismissed the case, which was again appealed to the 11th Circuit. The plaintiffs simultaneously petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court for injunctive relief, an “extraordinary request” they claimed was necessary in light of time constraints before the Electoral College met. The Supreme Court denied their motion to expedite the case, and the parties entered a stipulation of dismissal before the 11th Circuit and Supreme Court.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Democratic lawsuit challenging four Wisconsin laws during of the 2020 election cycle in light of the COVID-19 pandemic.
title: Wisconsin COVID-19 Election Relief
body:
Lawsuit filed ahead of the Wisconsin 2020 April primary election by the Democratic National Committee (DNC) and Democratic Party of Wisconsin challenging four state laws that plaintiffs allege severely burden the right to vote during the COVID-19 pandemic: the electronic and mail registration deadline, document and photo ID registration requirement, witness requirement and absentee ballot receipt deadline. The district court granted a preliminary injunction to extend the registration and ballot receipt deadline in this case and similar consolidated cases. The Wisconsin Legislature filed an emergency appeal of the preliminary injunction to the 7th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, which denied the Legislature’s motion to stay the district court’s preliminary injunction regarding the registration and ballot receipt deadline. The Wisconsin Legislature appealed this ruling to the U.S. Supreme Court, which stayed the district court’s preliminary injunction regarding the ballot receipt deadline extension.

After the April primary, the plaintiffs filed an amended complaint raising the same claims for the upcoming 2020 general election. The district court granted injunctive relief regarding multiple aspects of the registration and vote by mail process. The 7th Circuit stayed the district court’s preliminary injunction regarding the registration and ballot receipt deadline extensions, which the U.S. Supreme Court affirmed. After the Supreme Court’s ruling, the 7th Circuit dismissed the appeals and the parties entered a stipulation of dismissal in district court.

parties: Election Integrity Project of Nevada v. Nevada
excerpt: Conservative lawsuit challenging Nevada’s vote by mail plans for the 2020 general election in light of the COVID-19 pandemic.
title: Nevada Election Integrity Intervention
body: Lawsuit filed by the right-wing organization Election Integrity Project of Nevada challenging the state’s plan to mail ballots to all eligible voters ahead of the 2020 general election in light of the COVID-19 pandemic. The court denied the plaintiffs’ request for a preliminary injunction seeking to block the mailing of ballots. The plaintiffs unsuccessfully petitioned the Nevada Supreme Court and then filed for a second motion for a preliminary injunction in district court, which was also denied. The plaintiffs dismissed the case.

parties: Ziccarelli v. Allegheny County Board of Elections
excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to block the counting of certain ballots in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania.
title: Pennsylvania Allegheny County Certification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by Republican state Senate candidate seeking to block Allegheny County from including “undated” ballots in its certification of presidential election results. The court denied the plaintiff’s motion for a temporary restraining order and later granted summary judgment in favor of the defendants, finding that “the undated ballots at issue remain valid ballots that are properly counted under state law.”



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. v. Toulouse Oliver
excerpt: Trump lawsuit seeking to delay certification of New Mexico’s 2020 presidential election results.
title: New Mexico Certification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Trump campaign seeking to delay certification of New Mexico’s 2020 presidential election results and order a statewide canvass of absentee votes and an investigation of drop boxes. The Democratic National Committee (DNC) intervened in the case to oppose the Trump campaign’s motion for a preliminary injunction. The plaintiff voluntarily dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. v. Philadelphia County Board of Elections
excerpt: Trump campaign seeking to stop Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania from counting ballots without observers present.
title: Pennsylvania Philadelphia County BOE Vote Counting
body:
Lawsuit brought by the Trump campaign seeking to stop the Philadelphia County Board of Elections from counting ballots until Republican observers are present. The court denied the Trump campaign’s motion for an emergency injunction and the campaign voluntarily dismissed the case.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit alleging multiple fraud conspiracies related to the 2020 presidential election results in Michigan.
title: Michigan Detroit Election Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by individual voters alleging multiple fraud conspiracies related to the 2020 presidential election in Michigan. The complaint asks the board of elections to conduct an audit of the election, prohibit the certification of the election and order that a new election to be held. The trial court denied the plaintiffs’ request for injunctive relief and both the Michigan Court of Appeals and Supreme Court denied attempts to appeal. Back in the trial court, the plaintiffs filed a motion to audit election results, which was also denied. After the parties filed a stipulation of dismissal, the case was dismissed.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: On Jan. 8, 2021, the case was dismissed. Michigan’s 2020 presidential election results remain certified.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to decertify the 2020 presidential election results in Georgia.
title: Georgia Decertification Challenge #2
body:
Lawsuit filed by individual Georgia voter seeking to decertify the presidential election results in Georgia based on allegations of out-of-state voters unlawfully casting ballots in the state and signature verification issues. Biden electors for the state successfully intervened. The trial court dismissed the case for finding, among other things, that the allegations in the complaint “rest on speculation.” The Georgia Supreme Court denied an emergency petition and the individual Georgia voter then voluntarily dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Trump lawsuit challenging the 2020 presidential election results in Georgia.
title: Georgia Trump Election Contest
body:
Election contest filed by Donald Trump, the Trump campaign and a Trump elector challenging the presidential election results in Georgia based on allegations of “illegal votes.” During the course of normal case proceedings, the petitioners attempted to appeal a non-final order to the Georgia Supreme Court, claiming that the lower court judge was not “qualified to preside over” the case. The Georgia Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, and petitioners subsequently voluntarily dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to decertify Georgia’s 2020 presidential election results.
title: Georgia Election Contest (Coffee County)
body:
Election contest filed by two Georgia voters seeking to decertify the election results for both Coffee County and the entire state of Georgia based on unsubstantiated allegations of irregularity and fraud during the county’s recount. The complaint argues that these irregularities also affected the entire state’s election results. The plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Trump lawsuit seeking to decertify Georgia’s 2020 presidential election results.
title: Georgia Trump Decertification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by Donald Trump against Georgia’s governor and secretary of state seeking to decertify Georgia’s 2020 presidential election results based on alleged claims of “illegal voting.” Trump voluntarily dismissed the lawsuit.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit challenging North Carolina procedures for delivering, processing and curing absentee ballots.
title: North Carolina Four Pillars Intervention (Legislature)
body: Lawsuit brought by the speaker of the North Carolina House of Representatives challenging a consent decree entered in state court with the North Carolina State Board of Elections that extended ballot receipt deadlines, issued new cure guidance and expanded absentee ballot drop off locations. The North Carolina Alliance for Retired Americans and others intervened in the case to protect the consent decree’s expansion of voting rights during the COVID-19 pandemic. The U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina temporarily enjoined the enforcement of the state court’s consent decree before consolidating the case with Wise v. North Carolina State Board of Elections and transferring it to the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of North Carolina. The Middle District Court declined to grant the plaintiffs’ requested preliminary injunction. The 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed and the U.S. Supreme Court denied the application for injunctive relief filed by the Trump campaign. The plaintiffs then dismissed the case.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging inadequate early voting dates for the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections.
title: Georgia Runoff Early Vote (Paulding County)
body: Lawsuit brought by the New Georgia Project against Paulding County regarding its alleged failure to provide adequate early voting dates for Georgia Senate runoff elections. The case was voluntarily dismissed by NGP after the runoff elections.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging inadequate early voting dates for the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections.
title: Georgia Runoff Early Vote (Bibb County)
body: Lawsuit brought by the New Georgia Project against Bibb County regarding its alleged failure to provide adequate early voting dates for 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections. The case was voluntarily dismissed by the plaintiff after the runoff elections.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging inadequate early voting dates for the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections.
title: Georgia Runoff Early Vote (Clarke County)
body: Lawsuit brought by the New Georgia Project against Clarke County regarding its alleged failure to provide adequate early voting dates for the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections. The case was voluntarily dismissed by the plaintiff after the runoff elections.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging inadequate early voting dates for the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections.
title: Georgia Runoff Early Vote (Fulton County)
body: Lawsuit brought by the New Georgia Project against Fulton County regarding its alleged failure to provide adequate early voting dates for Georgia Senate runoff elections. The case was voluntarily dismissed by the plaintiff following the runoff elections.

parties: Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. v. Benson
excerpt: Trump lawsuit seeking to stop the counting of absentee ballots in the 2020 presidential election in Michigan.
title: Michigan Absentee Ballot Counting Intervention
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Trump campaign and an individual voter attempting to stop the counting of absentee ballots in Michigan. The Michigan Court of Claims denied the plaintiffs’ motion for declaratory judgment and both the state Court of Appeals and Supreme Court denied further appeal attempts.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: On Jan. 6, 2021, the Michigan Court of Claims dismissed the lawsuit as moot. Absentee ballots in Michigan were counted.

excerpt: Lawsuit filed by the Navajo Nation challenging Arizona’s ballot receipt deadline for mail-in ballots.
title: Arizona Navajo Nation Members Mail-in Ballot Challenge
body: Lawsuit filed by individual members of the Navajo Nation challenging Arizona’s ballot receipt deadline requiring mail-in ballots to be received (not postmarked) by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. The complaint alleges that this requirement burdens the right to vote for those, such as voters of the Navajo Nation, that rely on U.S. Postal Service to cast their ballots. The district court denied the plaintiffs’ motion for a preliminary injunction and declined to extend the ballot receipt deadline, finding that plaintiffs had not demonstrated a “disparate burden” on Navajo members living on-reservation, despite acknowledging that access to mail and other forms of voting may be more difficult for Navajo members. The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the district court’s decision and the case was dismissed.

parties: Schmitz v. Fulton County Board of Registration and Elections
excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to purge voters from Fulton County, Georgia’s rolls.
title: Georgia Fulton County Voter Purge
body: Petition filed by two Georgia residents attempting to purge over 14,000 voters from Fulton County’s rolls after the county’s election board declined to hold hearings on the suggested purges. The trial court dismissed the mandamus petition, which the petitioners appealed to the Georgia Court of Appeals. The Court of Appeals transferred the case to the Georgia Supreme Court, holding that it had exclusive jurisdiction, and the state Supreme Court dismissed the appeal.

state: The should-be state of District of Columbia
excerpt: Republican lawsuit challenging the outcome of the 2020 presidential election.
title: District of Columbia Trump Election Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by right-wing organizations and Republican voters and officials challenging the outcome of the 2020 presidential election due to the fact that state legislatures were unable to meet in person due to the COVID-19 pandemic to certify votes and presidential electors. The district court dismissed the case, finding, among other issues, that the “suit rests on a fundamental and obvious misreading of the Constitution.”



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit against Vice President Mike Pence challenging the constitutionality of the Electoral Count Act.
title: Texas Electoral Count Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by a Texas Republican congressman and Arizona’s Republican electoral college electors against Vice President Mike Pence challenging the constitutionality of the Electoral Count Act. Specifically, the plaintiffs asked that Vice President Pence be given the authority to determine electoral votes for each state. The district court dismissed the case for lack of subject matter jurisdiction, holding that none of the plaintiffs had standing to bring the case. The 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging the lack of early voting opportunities in Houston County, Georgia.
title: Georgia Runoff Early Vote (Houston County)
body: Lawsuit brought by the New Georgia Project against Houston County regarding its alleged failure to provide adequate early voting dates for Georgia Senate runoff elections. The plaintiffs filed a petition for a writ of mandamus as well as an emergency motion for a temporary restraining order asking the court to direct Houston County to allow more early voting dates. The trial court denied the plaintiffs’ petition and motion and the Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed.

parties: Republican National Committee v. State Election Board
excerpt: Republican lawsuit challenging several aspects of the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections.
title: Georgia Runoff Election Challenge #1
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Republican National Committee (RNC) and Georgia Republican Party challenging poll watcher access and the use of ballot drop boxes ahead of the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections. The Democratic Party of Georgia and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) moved in intervene in the case. The Superior Court of Fulton County dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to overturn the 2020 presidential election results in Dakota County, Minnesota.
title: Minnesota 2nd Congressional District Election Contest (Dakota County)
body:
Election contest filed in Dakota County by a group of Republican federal and state candidates and individual voters seeking to overturn the results of the 2020 general election. The contest claimed that the inclusion of absentee ballots in the county’s results was illegal. The contestants filed a second petition asking for permission to review physical ballots and voting machines. The state district court dismissed the case with prejudice. The contestants appealed to the Minnesota Supreme Court, but then voluntarily dismissed their appeal.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: On Dec. 24, 2020, the contestants voluntarily dismissed their appeal to the Minnesota Supreme Court. Minnesota’s 2020 general election results remain certified.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit challenging the signature verification process for the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections.
title: Georgia Runoff Election Challenge #3
body:
Lawsuit filed by Georgia Republican Party, National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) and the Perdue and Loeffler campaigns challenging the signature verification process for absentee ballots cast in the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections. The Democratic Party of Georgia and Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC) intervened in the case to protect the right of all Georgians to vote. After the district court dismissed the case, the Georgia Republican Party and other plaintiffs appealed to the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals but soon thereafter filed a voluntary notice of dismissal after their motion to stay (pause) the case pending appeal was denied.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to modify election administration practices ahead of the 2021 Georgia Senate runoff elections.
title: Georgia Runoff Election Challenge #4
body:
Lawsuit filed by Georgia Republican Party, National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC), the Perdue and Loeffler Senate campaigns and three voters seeking to prohibit people who voted for a Senate candidate in the 2020 election in a different state from voting in the Jan. 5 Georgia Senate runoff elections and to segregate all ballots cast by voters who registered to vote between Nov. 4 and Dec. 7, 2020. After the district court dismissed the case, the Georgia Republican Party and other plaintiffs appealed to the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals but soon thereafter filed a voluntary notice of dismissal.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Fair Fight v. True the Vote
excerpt: Lawsuit challenging third-party voter intimidation practices in Georgia.
title: Georgia Voter Intimidation Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed on behalf of Fair Fight and two voters challenging True the Vote’s alleged voter intimidation tactics in Georgia. The amended complaint argues that the defendants (True the Vote, True the Vote’s executive director and individuals who have acted in concert with True the Vote) violated Section 11(b) of the Voting Rights Act (VRA) by intimidating voters. The plaintiffs allege that the organization’s actions — which include challenging voters’ registration “on the basis of unreliable information,” “recruiting ‘citizen watchdogs’ to watch voters return their ballots” and “offering a $1 million reward to incentivize its supporters to find evidence of ‘illegal voting”’ — likely violate the VRA. The plaintiffs request that the court declare that the defendants violated Section 11(b) of the VRA, cancel True the Vote’s pending voter challenges, prevent True the Vote from submitting voter challenges in Georgia, prevent True the Vote from contacting voters, prevent True the Vote from participating in “in any poll-watching, poll-monitoring, or election observing activities; recruiting and training individuals for these activities; or advertising these activities,” prevent True the Vote from taking photos or videos of voters or election workers and order True the Vote to cease operations in Georgia.

In response to these allegations, True the Vote filed counterclaims against Fair Fight alleging the Fair Fight and its founder Stacey Abrams violated Section 11 (b) by intimidating True the Vote’s members. These counterclaims were dismissed on Aug. 17, 2021.

The case then proceeded to the summary judgment stage. In the plaintiffs’ motion for summary judgment, they allege that True the Vote recruited “former Navy SEALs to patrol polling stations,” amplified false claims, “expressed support for threatening rhetoric on social media” and that True the Vote’s mass challenge scheme intimidated voters. In response, the defendants suggest in their own summary judgment motion that: Section 11(b) requires “a direct connection between the person claiming to be intimidated and the alleged perpetrator,” a connection they argue doesn’t exist in the case. They also argue that applying Section 11(b) to their voter challenges would prohibit them from protecting their vote from vote dilution and assert that their actions are protected under the First Amendment so Section 11(b) is unconstitutional.

In January 2023, the U.S. Department of Justice accepted an invitation from the court to participate in the lawsuit given that the defendants questioned the constitutionality of Section 11(b). On Jan. 2, 2024, a federal judge ruled that the defendants did not violate Section 11(b) of the VRA.

STATUS: On Feb. 1, 2024, the plaintiffs appealed the decision to the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, where litigation is ongoing.

excerpt: Election contest challenging the winner of Iowa’s 2nd District in the 2020 election.
title: Iowa 2nd Congressional District Election Contest
body: Election contest filed by congressional candidate Rita Hart (D) in the U.S. House of Representatives challenging the certification of the 2020 general election results for Iowa’s 2nd Congressional District. Hart later withdrew her challenge.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to overturn the 2020 general election results in three Michigan congressional districts.
title: Minnesota Congressional District Election Contests (Ramsey County)
body:
Election contests filed in Ramsey County by a group of Republican candidates and individual voters seeking to overturn the results of the 2020 general election in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th Congressional Districts due to baseless allegations of fraud. The court dismissed all the contests.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: The court dismissed all the election contests on Dec. 18, 2020. Minnesota’s 2020 general election results remain certified.

excerpt: Democratic lawsuit challenging South Carolina’s vote by mail restrictions ahead of the 2020 general election.
title: South Carolina COVID-19 Election Relief (Vote By Mail)
body: Lawsuit filed on behalf of individual voters, the South Carolina Democratic Party, Democratic National Committee (DNC) and Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) challenging South Carolina’s vote by mail restrictions ahead of the 2020 general election, specifically: the witness requirement for absentee ballots, lack of prepaid postage for mail-in ballots, ballot receipt deadline and ballot collection ban. As a result of the lawsuit, South Carolina agreed to provide prepaid postage for all mail-in ballots for the 2020 general election, likely saving voters over $1 million on postage. The district court struck down the witness requirement for absentee voting, but denied plaintiffs’ request for injunctive relief as to the other vote by mail restrictions. The en banc 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals voted 9-5 to affirm the district court’s order striking down the witness requirement, but the U.S. Supreme Court stayed the decision. The parties later dismissed the appeal.

excerpt: Democratic lawsuit challenging South Carolina’s lack of cure opportunities to fix mail-in ballots with certain deficiencies.
title: South Carolina Cure Guidance
body: Lawsuit filed on behalf of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee and an individual voter challenging South Carolina’s lack of cure opportunities for mail-in ballots with alleged signature or witness requirement deficiencies. After the district court granted a preliminary injunction in a case raising related issues, the state was prohibited from disqualifying otherwise valid ballots based on mismatched signatures without providing notice and an opportunity to cure. After the state released new signature matching guidance, the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed this case.

excerpt: Lawsuit brought by Texas against Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Georgia and Michigan seeking to invalidate their election results.
title: Texas SCOTUS Decertification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit brought by the state of Texas against Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Georgia and Michigan seeking to invalidate their election results. Texas petitioned the U.S. Supreme Court, which denied its request for lack of standing.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging provisions of the 1890 Mississippi Constitution regarding the state’s election system.
title: Mississippi Election System
body: Lawsuit filed by individual voters challenging provisions of the 1890 Mississippi Constitution that required a candidate for statewide office to win a majority of both the popular vote and state House districts in order to be elected. The framers originally devised this system with the explicit purpose of diluting Black votes, which the complaint alleges violates the 14th and 15th Amendments and Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. As a response to this litigation, the state Legislature proposed an amendment to repeal the discriminatory election scheme, which was passed by voters in the 2020 general election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to decertify the 2020 presidential election results in Pennsylvania.
title: Pennsylvania Decertification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by a group of Republican state representatives and two Republican voters seeking to decertify the 2020 general election results in Pennsylvania. The court denied the plaintiffs’ emergency motion for injunctive relief, finding that the action was an “improper and untimely election contest,” and the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit challenging Minnesota’s extension of its ballot receipt deadline.
title: Minnesota Receipt Deadline Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by Republican electors for Minnesota challenging the extension of the mail-in ballot receipt deadline agreed to in a previous lawsuit due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The complaint alleges that the extension violates the U.S. Constitution and asks the court to block the Minnesota secretary of state from accepting ballots received after Election Day. The district court denied the plaintiffs’ motion for a preliminary injunction seeking to block the counting of post-Election Day ballots and dismissed the case, holding that the plaintiffs did not have standing to bring the case.

RESULT: The Republican electors appealed to the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, which reversed the district court’s ruling that the plaintiffs did not have standing and also blocked the deadline extension from taking effect.

excerpt: Conservative lawsuit seeking to delay certification of Michigan’s 2020 presidential election results.
title: Michigan Thomas More Society Election Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Thomas More Society, a conservative legal group, asking the Michigan Supreme Court to segregate ballots and delay Michigan’s certification of its 2020 presidential election results. The court denied the petition’s request for declaratory relief.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: On Dec. 9, 2020, the court denied the Thomas More Society’s challenge. Michigan’s 2020 presidential election results remain in place.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to nullify the 2020 presidential election results in Georgia.
title: Georgia Election Law Contest
body:
Election contest filed by a right-wing group on behalf of an individual voter seeking to nullify the presidential election results in Georgia and block the state from certifying the results so that the Georgia General Assembly could appoint electors. Biden electors for the state successfully intervened. The court granted the defendants’ motion to dismiss.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Trump lawsuit alleging voter fraud in Nevada.
title: Nevada Election Law Contest
body:
Election contest filed by individual Trump electors in Nevada alleging voter fraud in the state due to the signature matching machines used to count ballots. The state district court granted the defendants’ motion to dismiss, finding that the contestants failed to provide “credible and relevant evidence” to support their allegations of fraud. The contestants appealed the decision to the Nevada Supreme Court, which affirmed the district court.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. v. Bucks County Board of Elections
excerpt: Trump petition challenging Bucks County, Pennsylvania’s decision to count certain mail-in ballots.
title: Pennsylvania Bucks County BOE Appeal
body:
Petition filed by the Trump campaign, Republican National Committee (RNC) and Republican campaigns appealing the Bucks County Board of Elections’ (BOE) decision to count certain mail-in ballots that petitioners believed to be deficient, such as ballots returned without a sealed privacy ballot or ballots with incomplete dates or addresses. The Democratic National Committee (DNC) successfully intervened in the case to defend vote by mail. The trial court and appellate court affirmed the BOE’s decision to count the ballots and the Pennsylvania Supreme Court rejected the Republicans’ petition to appeal the lower courts’ decisions.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to vacate the certification of 2020 presidential election results in Arizona.
title: Arizona Election Contest #2
body:
Lawsuit brought by Republican voters against Gov. Doug Ducey (R) and Arizona Secretary of State Katie Hobbs (D) seeking to vacate the certification of the 2020 presidential election in Arizona. The plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Wisconsin Voters Alliance v. Wisconsin Elections Commission
excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to block certification of the 2020 presidential election results in Wisconsin.
title: Wisconsin Certification Challenge
body:
Petition filed by Wisconsin Voters Alliance and individual voters against the Wisconsin Elections Commission asking the Wisconsin Supreme Court to nullify and block certification of the results of the Wisconsin presidential election and allow the state’s legislature to appoint electors. The Wisconsin Supreme Court denied the petition.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to delay certification of the 2020 presidential election results in Minnesota.
title: Minnesota Election Certification Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by Minnesota state legislators, candidates and individual voters seeking to delay the certification of the presidential election results in the state. The Minnesota Supreme Court dismissed the petition.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: On Dec. 4, 2020, the Minnesota Supreme Court dismissed the petition. Minnesota’s 2020 general election results were certified.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to block the certification of 2020 presidential election results in Wisconsin.
title: Wisconsin Election Results Challenge
body:
Petition filed by an individual Wisconsin voter against the Wisconsin Elections Commission (WEC) seeking to block the certification of the 2020 presidential election results based on allegations that absentee ballots placed in drop boxes were “illegal.” The petitioner asked the court to allow the Wisconsin Legislature to arrange another election before election results were certified (December 14) or appoint ten electoral college electors for the state. The Wisconsin Supreme Court denied the petition.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Trump lawsuit challenging the inclusion of certain absentee ballots in Wisconsin’s 2020 presidential election results.
title: Wisconsin Absentee Count Challenge
body:
Petition filed by President Donald Trump, Vice President Mike Pence and the Trump campaign challenging the validity and inclusion of certain absentee ballots in the state’s presidential election results. The Wisconsin Supreme Court denied the petition.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Tennessee Conference of the NAACP v. Lee
excerpt: Class action lawsuit filed on behalf of the Tennessee State Conference of the NAACP and five individuals — who attempted to restore their right to vote before the November 2020 election and were denied — against Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee (R), Secretary of State Tre Hargett (R) and other state and county officials.
title: Tennessee Class Action Voting Rights Restoration Lawsuit
body:
Class action lawsuit filed on behalf of the Tennessee State Conference of the NAACP and five individuals — who attempted to restore their right to vote before the November 2020 election and were denied — against Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee (R), Secretary of State Tre Hargett (R) and other state and county officials.

The lawsuit challenges Tennessee’s inaccessible and non-uniform method for restoring voting rights to individuals with prior felony convictions. In order to restore one’s voting rights in Tennessee, residents who meet specific criteria can request a Certificate of Restoration of Voting Rights (COR) from the Governor or the Tennessee Department of Corrections, and then submit the COR to the county election administrator. The lawsuit alleges that some plaintiffs have requested CORs and have not received them or have been in situations where there is no mechanism for the individual to obtain a COR.

The complaint argues that the implementation of Tennessee’s rights restoration process creates “an unequal, scattershot system across Tennessee’s ninety-five counties, causing disparate results for similarly situated individuals,” and at least one county, Rutherford County, charges a fee for the COR. The complaint asserts that this fee constitutes a poll tax and violates the 24th Amendment. The complaint also alleges that the state’s arbitrary scheme for restoring voting rights violates the Due Process and Equal Protection Clauses of the 14th Amendment and that elements of Tennessee’s voter registration process violate the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA).

According to the lawsuit, “Tennessee’s felony disenfranchisement law continues to have a disparate impact on Black Tennesseans. Black people make up 16% of the state’s total voting-age population, but account for 39% of its disenfranchised population. Of the state’s 451,000 disenfranchised citizens, nearly 175,000 are Black, accounting for more than 21% of the Black voting-age population—one of the highest rates of Black disenfranchisement in the United States.”

The plaintiffs ask the court to order the implementation of a uniform, formal method to request a COR (without a fee) “before an impartial decision maker” and to require the creation of voter “registration forms and policies that comply with the NVRA.”

In 2023, Tennessee filed an appeal to the 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals arguing the district court wrongly certified the Tennessee NACCP’s lawsuit as a class action. On Feb. 8, 2024, the 6th Circuit remanded the case and ordered the district court to hold further proceedings to resolve the question of class certification.

On April 18, 2024, the judge denied in part and granted in part motions for summary judgment.

On June 7, 2024, the Tennessee governor appealed that decision to the 6th Circuit.

On June 28, 2024, the 6th Circuit granted a motion to stay the district court’s injunction. Oral argument is tentatively scheduled to begin on Oct. 28, 2024. The state’s felony disenfranchisement policies will remain in effect while the appeal is ongoing.

STATUS: Oral argument before the 6th Circuit is scheduled for Jan. 14, 2025.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking a new election in Nevada based on allegations of faulty ballot processing machines.
title: Nevada Mail Ballot Machine Challenge #1
body:
Lawsuit filed by a Republican state Senate candidate requesting a new election based on allegations that the machines used to process mail-in ballots were faulty. The Democratic National Committee (DNC) and Nevada State Democratic Party intervened in the case and the court granted their motion to dismiss.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to stop the certification of certain 2020 presidential results in Pennsylvania.
title: Pennsylvania Presidential Elector Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by individual voters seeking to stop the certification of presidential election results from certain Pennsylvania counties based on claims that “illegal” ballots were included. The plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking a new election in Nevada based on allegations of faulty ballot processing machines.
title: Nevada Mail Ballot Machine Challenge #4
body:
Lawsuit filed by a Republican congressional candidate requesting a new election based on allegations that the machines used to process mail-in ballots were faulty. The Nevada State Democratic Party intervened in the case and the court granted its motion to dismiss.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit challenging the use of mail-in ballot processing machines in Clark County, Nevada.
title: Nevada Vote Count Halt (Clark County)
body:
Lawsuit filed by individual voters and Republican candidate committees seeking access to the ballot counting process and challenging the use of mail-in ballot processing machines used in Clark County on the basis that the signature matching technology is faulty. The Democratic National Committee (DNC) and Nevada State Democratic Party intervened in the case, pointing out that nearly identical lawsuits claiming voter fraud and illegal lack of access to view ballot counting had been tossed out days prior. The court denied the plaintiffs’ motion for injunctive relief and the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking a new election in Nevada based on allegations of faulty ballot processing machines.
title: Nevada Mail Ballot Machine Challenge #2
body:
Lawsuit filed by a Republican congressional candidate requesting a new election based on allegations that the machines used to process mail-in ballots were faulty. The Nevada State Democratic Party intervened in the case and the court denied the plaintiff’s petition for a writ of mandamus and dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging Michigan’s ballot receipt deadline extension and allowance of ballot collection.
title: Michigan Vote By Mail Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by individual voters challenging Michigan’s extension of the mail-in ballot receipt deadline and allowance of ballot collection for the 2020 general election. The Michigan Alliance for Retired Americans and the Detroit/Downriver chapter of the A. Philip Randolph Institute intervened in the case to protect the expansion of vote by mail options in the state.

RESULT: On Sept. 29, 2020, the parties entered a stipulation of voluntary dismissal. Michigan’s mail-in ballot receipt deadline remains in place.

parties: In re: Canvass of Absentee and Mail-In Ballots of November 3, 2020 General Election
excerpt: Trump petition challenging Philadelphia County, Pennsylvania’s decision to count certain absentee and mail-in ballots.
title: Pennsylvania Philadelphia County BOE Appeal
body:
Petition filed by the Trump campaign appealing the Philadelphia County Board of Elections’ (BOE) decision to count five different categories of around 8,000 absentee and mail-in ballots: those that are missing handwritten names, street addresses, dates or some combination of the three on the outer return envelope of the ballot. The trial court upheld the Philadelphia County BOE’s decision to count the ballots, finding that the omission of the challenged information does not promote fraud. The Trump campaign appealed this decision, but the Philadelphia County BOE moved to transfer the case to the Pennsylvania Supreme Court to exercise the court’s “extraordinary jurisdiction.” The state Supreme Court granted the application and affirmed the trial court’s decision upholding the Philadelphia County BOE’s inclusion of the challenged ballots.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Ziccarelli v. Allegheny County Board of Elections
excerpt: Republican petition challenging Allegheny County, Pennsylvania’s decision to count certain mail-in ballots.
title: Pennsylvania Allegheny County BOE Appeal
body:
Petition for review filed by Republican state Senate candidate appealing the Allegheny County Board of Elections’ decision to count mail-in ballots containing “undated voter declarations.” The trial court affirmed the BOE’s decision and denied the petition for review, finding that the ballots were sufficient. The candidate immediately petitioned the Pennsylvania Supreme Court for “extraordinary relief,” while also appealing the decision to the state appellate court. The state appellate court reversed the trial court, but the Pennsylvania Supreme Court reversed the appellate court in finding that the challenged ballots were valid.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking a new election in Nevada based on allegations of faulty ballot processing machines.
title: Nevada Mail Ballot Machine Challenge #3
body:
Lawsuit filed by Republican state Senate candidate against the Democratic incumbent requesting a new election based on allegations that the machines used to process mail-in ballots were faulty. The plaintiff voluntarily dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Ziccarelli v. Allegheny County Board of Elections
excerpt: Republican lawsuit challenging Allegheny County, Pennsylvania’s decision to count certain provisional ballots.
title: Pennsylvania Allegheny County BOE Appeal #2
body:
Petition filed by a Republican candidate for Pennsylvania state Senate appealing the Allegheny Board of Elections’ decision to count about 300 provisional ballots where voters signed in only one of two required places, often at the direction of an elections official. The Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania reversed the BOE’s decision, ordering it to exclude the challenged ballots from the county’s certified results.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging a Minnesota law regarding special elections for vacant seats.
title: Minnesota 2nd Congressional District Postponed Election
body:
Lawsuit filed by Rep. Angela Craig (D) and an individual voter challenging a Minnesota law that meant votes for the 2nd Congressional District would not be counted in the general election following the death of a major party candidate, leaving the seat open until a later special election.

RESULT: The district court granted a preliminary injunction that ordered the Minnesota secretary of state to count all ballots cast for the 2nd Congressional District. The 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed.

parties: Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. v. Benson
excerpt: Trump lawsuit challenging the ballot processing procedures in Wayne County, Michigan.
title: Michigan Wayne County Results Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Trump campaign and individual voters challenging the process by which Wayne County, Michigan processed ballots and its prohibition on challengers viewing the election tabulation process. The complaint seeks to enjoin the certification of any “fraudulent or unlawfully cast ballots.”

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: The plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case on Nov. 19, 2020. Wayne County, Michigan’s 2020 presidential election results remain certified.

parties: In re: Canvass of Absentee and Mail-in Ballots of November 3, 2020 General Election
excerpt: Trump lawsuit seeking to stop Montgomery County, Pennsylvania from counting certain mail-in ballots.
title: Pennsylvania Montgomery County BOE Vote Count
body:
Lawsuit filed by the Trump campaign, Republican National Committee and Republican campaigns seeking to stop the Montgomery County Board of Elections from counting mail-in ballots, claiming that certain voters did not properly write their addresses underneath their signatures on the outer envelopes. The trial court denied the petition for review and the Trump campaign withdrew its appeal to the appellate court.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit challenging the 2020 presidential election results in Georgia.
title: Georgia Democratic Counties Election Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by voters in Georgia claiming that election officials included “illegal Presidential Elector results” from certain Democratic-leaning counties in the state’s final election results. The challenge sought to to stop the certification of presidential election results from named counties. The Democratic Party of Georgia filed a motion to intervene in the case, but all pending motions were not ruled on as the plaintiffs filed a voluntary dismissal only five days after docketing the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit alleging that Wisconsin election officials included illegal presidential elector results in the statewide results.
