body:
Lawsuit filed by individual voters alleging that Wisconsin election officials included illegal presidential elector votes in certain Democratic counties. The suit asks the court to block the certification of presidential election results from the named counties. The Democratic National Committee (DNC) moved to intervene in the case, which plaintiffs then voluntarily dismissed.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

parties: Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. v. Hobbs
excerpt: Republican lawsuit alleging that ballots cast in Arizona using a Sharpie were not counted by ballot processing machines.
title: Arizona Trump Sharpie Lawsuit
body:
Lawsuit brought by the Trump campaign, Republican National Committee and Arizona Republican Party against the Arizona secretary of state alleging that ballots completed with a Sharpie were not counted by the ballot processing machines — a claim that proliferated on social media despite county officials strongly denying it. This lawsuit was identical to Aguilera v. Fontes, a case that had been voluntarily dismissed before this case was filed. The court dismissed the case with prejudice after holding an evidentiary hearing.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit seeking to exclude certain counties’ 2020 presidential election results from Michigan’s final election results.
title: Michigan Democratic Counties Election Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by individual voters seeking to exclude presidential election results in Wayne, Washtenaw and Ingham counties from Michigan’s 2020 general election results based on allegations that illegal ballots were counted. The plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.

This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

RESULT: On Nov. 16, 2020, the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed their complaint. Wayne, Washtenaw and Ingham counties’ results will be included in Michigan’s final 2020 general election results.

parties: Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. v. Boockvar
excerpt: Trump lawsuit attempting to prohibit Pennsylvania voters from providing proof of missing ID.
title: Pennsylvania Missing ID
body:
Lawsuit brought by the Trump campaign and Republican National Committee attempting to prohibit voters from providing proof of missing identification. The Democratic National Committee (DNC) intervened in the case. The court ruled that the Pennsylvania secretary of state did not have the authority to add three extra days to provide proof of ID and granted an injunction enjoining the county from counting ballots with IDs provided during that time frame.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Lawsuit filed by Kathy Barnette (R) and a voter against the Montgomery County Board of Elections alleging that the board began illegally pre-canvassing mail-in ballots and contacted voters to give them the opportunity to fix minor defects on their ballots.
title: Pennsylvania Mail-in Ballot Canvassing Challenge
body:
Lawsuit filed by Kathy Barnette (R), the Republican candidate for Pennsylvania’s 4th Congressional District, and a voter against the Montgomery County Board of Elections alleging that the board began illegally pre-canvassing (meaning tallying) mail-in ballots and contacted voters to give them the opportunity to fix minor defects (such as a missing signature) on their ballots. The plaintiffs argue that, under Pennsylvania law, “counties [are prohibited] from pre-canvasing any ballots, including absentee and mail-in ballots, before 7:00 a.m. on Election Day.” The plaintiffs also claim that “the Montgomery County Board of Elections is restricting the ability of candidates and their representatives…and other legally constituted watchers…to observe the entire canvass process for the mail-in and absentee ballots.” The plaintiffs assert that the defendant is violating the Equal Protection Clause of 14th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution because “equivalent votes in different counties and amongst similarly situated Montgomery County electors are being treated differently.” The plaintiffs ask the court to declare the defendants’ conduct unconstitutional and to void “any mail-in or absentee ballots that have been changed by an elector or otherwise not conforming with the Election Code.”

On Nov. 6, 2020, the court denied the plaintiffs’ motion for a temporary restraining order against the defendants. On Nov. 11, 2020, the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the lawsuit.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Trump campaign lawsuit seeking observation of ballot processing in Clark County, Nevada.
title: Nevada Ballot Observation Intervention
body: Lawsuit filed by an individual voter, the Trump campaign and Nevada Republican Party attempting to prohibit the processing and counting of ballots in Clark County until “meaningful observation” of the process is allowed. The district court denied the plaintiffs’ motion for a temporary restraining order, which they appealed to the state Supreme Court. The Nevada Supreme Court also denied the plaintiffs’ motion for injunctive relief. The parties reached a settlement agreement and the Nevada Supreme Court dismissed the appeal.

parties: Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. v. Gloria
excerpt: Trump lawsuit seeking to extend polling place hours in Clark County, Nevada due to technical problems on Election Day.
title: Nevada Polling Place Extension
body: Lawsuit filed by the Trump campaign and Nevada Republican Party asking the court to direct the Clark County registrar to keep polls open an hour past normal closing times due to delays earlier in the day caused by technical problems. The court ordered the affected polling places to remain open until 8 p.m. and the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.

excerpt: Democratic lawsuit challenging Florida’s ballot order statute.
title: Florida Ballot Order
body: Lawsuit filed by individual voters, Priorities USA, Democratic National Committee (DNC), Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC), Democratic Governors Association (DGA) and Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee (DLCC) challenging Florida’s ballot order statute, which requires that candidates of the political party of the governor be listed first on the ballot in all elections. The complaint alleges that this statute treats similarly situated candidates differently without sufficient justification and violates the First and 14th Amendments. The district court ruled in favor of the plaintiffs, finding that the ballot order statute violates the First and 14th Amendments by taking “a side in partisan elections.” Republican intervenor-defendants appealed the decision to the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, which vacated the district court’s judgment and remanded the case with instructions to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction.

title: Arizona Public Interest Ballot Cure
body:
Lawsuit filed by individual Republican voters alleging that ballots cast in Arizona using a Sharpie were not counted — a claim that proliferated on social media despite county officials strongly denying it. The plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case.



This case was one of the lawsuits former President Donald Trump and his allies brought in an effort to overturn the results of the 2020 election.

excerpt: Republican lawsuit seeking to block the casting of certain provisional ballots in Pennsylvania.
title: Pennsylvania Provisional Ballot Challenge
body: Lawsuit filed on Election Day by Republican candidates and individual voters seeking to block voters whose mail-in ballots were rejected from also casting provisional ballots. The Democratic National Committee (DNC) intervened in the case. The court granted a partial preliminary injunction, stating that provisional ballots cast on Election Day by an individual whose absentee ballot was received in time must be segregated. The court rejected the petitioners’ other requests.

title: Pennsylvania Northampton County Ballots
body: Lawsuit filed by Northampton County Republican Committee attempting to stop the county board of elections from disclosing the identity of cancelled ballots. The plaintiff voluntarily withdrew its appeal.

parties: In re: Enforcement of Election Laws
